extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of literary fiction; creative writers
extracted.subtask_description: Close-reading and appreciation of a midwestern literary-prose excerpt (William H. Gass). Useful for literary analysis, stylistic study, and creative-writing reflection on voice, imagery, and embodiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry's purpose — to bring within about, to change
rubrics_metrics.description: For that is poetry: to bring within about, to change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrator frames poetry as an act of transformation — bringing the outside world into the page and altering perception. Surrounding lines emphasize intensity of gaze and the desire to make an image 'bloom' on the page; poetry's effect is to change the reader's view by transposing experience into language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on embodiment — 'body equals being'
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry, like love, is—in and out—da physical caress. Body equals being, and if your weight goes down, you are the less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text asserts that poetic truth and vitality are rooted in bodily experience and sensual immediacy rather than abstract 'spirit.' This suggests a criterion for writing grounded, embodied language and physical detail; the narrator rejects disembodied sophistries and values concrete, tactile imagery and sensation.
